Program Overview
The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Neuroscience at MUSC is a residential program designed to help you build the knowledge, research experience and scientific independence needed for a career in neuroscience. You’ll study the brain and nervous system across molecular, cellular, circuit and behavioral levels while exploring areas such as addiction neuroscience, neurodegenerative disease, neurodevelopmental disorders and neuro oncology.
Through advanced coursework, laboratory rotations, faculty mentorship and dissertation research, you’ll learn to design studies, analyze complex data, evaluate scientific evidence and communicate findings clearly. This training can support career paths in academic research, biotechnology, pharmaceutical development, government science, computational neuroscience and translational research. As your interests develop, you’ll have opportunities to refine your research focus, identify a mentor and build expertise that aligns with your professional goals. Explore the learning experience, research disciplines and faculty who can help shape your path forward.

Inside the Program
The Ph.D. in Neuroscience prepares you to investigate how the nervous system shapes health, behavior and disease. In this residential, research intensive program, you will build scientific independence through rigorous study, faculty mentorship, laboratory rotations and sustained research spanning molecular, cellular, systems and behavioral neuroscience.
Skills you will gain
Through coursework, scientific literature and immersive research, you will learn to frame original questions, design rigorous studies and select experimental, analytical or computational methods that fit the problem. You will strengthen your ability to interpret complex data, evaluate evidence, communicate findings and adapt your approach as new results guide discovery.
Support for your success
You will learn in a collaborative academic health sciences community with space to explore and refine your interests. Laboratory rotations help you compare research settings and mentoring approaches before selecting a faculty mentor. Seminars, journal clubs, core facilities and constructive feedback support your growth from guided learning toward independent scholarship.
Who should apply
This program is well suited for curious, research focused applicants who want to understand the brain and nervous system and contribute to advances in health. It is a strong fit for students with research experience who seek intensive doctoral preparation for careers in scientific discovery, education and leadership.
Disciplines
The Ph.D. in Neuroscience program gives you the flexibility to examine the nervous system through multiple scientific lenses. Depending on your research interests and faculty mentor, you may focus your training in one of four disciplines:
Addiction Neuroscience: Explore how brain systems related to reward, stress, learning and decision making contribute to substance use disorders. You’ll study biological mechanisms that may inform future approaches to prevention, treatment and recovery.
Neurodegenerative Disease: Investigate the cellular, molecular and systems level changes that contribute to progressive neurological conditions. You’ll examine disease mechanisms that may support future diagnostic and therapeutic discoveries.
Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Study how changes in brain development affect nervous system function, behavior and long term health. You’ll examine the molecular, cellular and circuit level processes that contribute to developmental neurological conditions.
Neuro-Oncology: Examine cancers that affect the brain, spinal cord and nervous system through a neuroscience and biomedical sciences lens. You’ll study tumor biology, disease mechanisms and treatment related discoveries that may improve future patient outcomes.
Together, these disciplines allow you to connect foundational neuroscience with research questions that advance understanding of neurological health, disease and discovery.

Research Experience
Research is central to your experience in the Ph.D. in Neuroscience program. Through laboratory rotations, faculty guided projects, seminars and dissertation work, you’ll gain hands on training that prepares you to ask meaningful questions about the brain, nervous system and neurological disease.
Early research experiences help you explore mentor fit, develop technical skills and identify the scientific questions that will shape your doctoral training. As you advance, you’ll work closely with faculty mentors to design experiments, analyze data, interpret findings and share your work through presentations, publications and scholarly discussion.
This research centered approach helps you grow from guided learning to independent investigation while building the scientific judgment, resilience and technical expertise needed for careers in academic, clinical, industry or translational research environments.

Eligibility Requirements
All applicants must:
Possess, or expect to have earned, a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in the U.S. or its equivalent from a foreign institution prior to enrolling
Submitted a GradCAS application
Submission of a standardized test score is not required but will be considered if submitted.
No single metric is used to assess applicants, but rather a broader picture of the candidate’s equalities is considered by our admissions committee. As a guideline, candidates with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or greater are more likely to be considered favorably.
Minimum Abilities
At MUSC, we actively support all students to ensure their success in both academic and clinical settings. To support this goal, the university outlines the essential qualities and functional abilities required for participation in its educational programs. These include a range of observational, communication, motor, intellectual and behavioral skills necessary for safe and effective practice.

Application Process
The following outlines the admissions process and what applicants can expect after submitting their application.
Submit your GradCAS application as early as possible. All application materials, including transcripts, letters of recommendation, and program-specific requirements, must be received by the final application deadline.
Complete the MUSC Supplemental Application. After submitting your GradCAS application, you will receive instructions for accessing and completing the MUSC Supplemental Application. Both the GradCAS application and MUSC Supplemental Application must be submitted before your application can be reviewed.
Application Review. Once all required materials have been received, the Graduate Admissions Committee will begin reviewing applications.
Virtual Faculty Interviews. Selected applicants will participate in virtual interviews with expert faculty members.
Campus Visit Invitations. Following the virtual interview process, a subset of applicants may be invited to campus to meet faculty, interact with current students, tour research facilities and learn more about the graduate experience at MUSC.
Final Admissions Decision. Following the campus visits, the Graduate Admissions Committee will complete its review and make final admissions recommendations. Applicants will be notified directly regarding their admission status.
On-campus visits take place in January and March.
Application Requirements
All applicants must submit a GradCAS application, which includes:
Letters of recommendation: All applicants must provide three letters of recommendation, preferably from instructors or supervisors in a scientific or health care position.
Official transcripts from all institutions attended. Applicants are required to submit unofficial or official transcripts for each and every post-secondary institution attended even if listed as transfer credit on another transcript. In cases where we accept unofficial documents, the unofficial document must be a copy of the original. If submitting an unofficial transcript, all courses, grades, degrees awarded (if applicable), and the name of the institution must be clearly visible on the document. Some academic advising reports and degree audits do not contain all the necessary information so the document should be reviewed before submission. If offered a position, the applicant will be asked to request an official transcript from each institution listed in the Education section of their application, regardless of the number of credit hours earned. MUSC reserves the right to rescind any offer of admission if any discrepancies are found between the unofficial and official transcripts.
Personal statement: All applicants must submit a personal statement, not to exceed 1,000 words, which explains their career goals and reasons for applying to the program.
Resume/CV: Applicants must provide an updated resume detailing relevant academic and professional experiences.
Note: If an applicant is unable to apply online, they must petition the Office of the Dean for special accommodation explaining why they are unable to apply online.
International Applicants
Academic records from foreign institutions must be provided in English, certified, and validated as authentic by a university or government official. The College of Graduate Studies requires that transcripts be evaluated by professional agencies and are submitted to MUSC electronically or in unopened envelopes showing the equivalency of work completed outside the U.S. The following websites are preferred agencies and are members of the National Association for Credit Evaluation Services (NACES). Their costs vary across agencies, and we encourage you to compare prices and select the best choice for you. NACES International Education Research Foundation – Credential Evaluation & Translation Services – Chartered NACES Member World Education Services: International Credential Evaluation for U.S. (wes.org) If your education was completed in the U.S., you do not need to complete a transcript credit evaluation.
If offered a position, and the applicant has only submitted an unofficial transcript evaluation, the candidate will be required to provide an official transcript and evaluation before any further consideration of that applicant will be given.
A language proficiency test is required for all applicants whose native language is not English. Scores must not be more than two years old. Exceptions can be made if a student has attended a United States institution for an extended period. An exception might also be made for students in a foreign institution that uses English as the primary language for instruction, however, these are made on a case-by-case basis.
Final consideration cannot be granted to an international student’s application for admission until these official scores are received by the Office of Enrollment Management. Accepted tests are IELTS and TOEFL. Minimal requirements are: TOEFL: 100 IELTS: 7
MUSC welcomes international applicants and offers tailored guidance to support you throughout the admission process. View details at International Applicants.

Cost of Attendance
The Cost of Attendance, or COA, estimates the total educational expenses for an enrollment period. The information below reflects the 2026-27 academic year. The COA includes direct costs, such as tuition and fees, billed by the university, as well as indirect costs you may need to plan for, including housing, food, transportation, books and other personal expenses.
For most admitted residential Ph.D. students, the COA does not reflect what you should expect to pay out of pocket. Tuition, health insurance and a stipend are generally provided as part of the student's funding package. Instead, the COA helps determine the maximum amount a student may borrow in an academic year and supports funding-related determinations, such as grants, scholarships, loans and others.
Your actual expenses may be lower than the COA, especially with careful budgeting. MUSC's Office of Student Financial Literacy can help you create a budget that supports your education, personal needs and long-term financial goals.

Scholarships & Aid
MUSC offers scholarships for which you may be eligible. Some are awarded based on academic achievement; others are awarded based on community service, for example. However, the majority of scholarships awarded at MUSC are based on financial need. This means that these scholarships are only awarded to students who need some financial assistance to cover the cost of tuition and fees. If you would like to be considered for a financial need-based scholarship, you must have an up-to-date Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) on file. Make sure you list the Medical University of South Carolina on your FAFSA form, along with MUSC's code: 003438. We encourage you to submit your FAFSA as early as possible. It is recommended to submit your FAFSA in January if you plan to enroll in the fall.
View scholarship opportunities
Annual Stipend
Students in the Ph.D. in Neuroscience program at MUSC receive a $39,000 annual stipend, effective July 1, 2026. The program also covers tuition, fees and health insurance for these students.

Frequently Asked Questions
Expand All
Is this a Doctor of Philosophy in Neuroscience?
addremove
Yes. You’ll earn a Ph.D. in Neuroscience while completing advanced research training focused on the brain, nervous system and neurological disease.
Do I need prior research experience to apply?
addremove
While formal prerequisites are not required, you should be prepared to show evidence of research experience or explain how your coursework, extracurricular activities, employment or other experiences reflect curiosity, readiness for doctoral-level inquiry and commitment to research training.
How do students choose a lab or mentor?
addremove
You’ll use laboratory rotations and early research experiences to explore faculty research, mentoring styles and potential dissertation directions. These rotation experiences help you identify the lab environment and mentor that best aligns with your research interests and career goals.
What kind of research could I pursue?
addremove
You may pursue research in nervous system function, neurological health, neurodevelopment, neuroplasticity, neuropsychiatric or neurodegenerative disease, computational neuroscience, translational neuroscience or other areas aligned with your faculty mentor.

Objectives
The Ph.D. in Neuroscience program aims to prepare graduates to:
Conduct independent research that advances understanding of the nervous system in health and disease
Integrate molecular, cellular, systems, behavioral and computational perspectives to address complex neuroscience questions
Design rigorous studies that produce reproducible and meaningful evidence
Communicate discoveries clearly to scientific, healthcare and public audiences
Lead collaborative research with ethical judgment, intellectual curiosity and respect for varied perspectives
Competencies
Upon completion of the Ph.D. in Neuroscience program, graduates will be able to:
Formulate original, testable questions grounded in critical evaluation of neuroscience literature
Select and apply appropriate experimental, analytical and computational methods
Interpret complex data, assess limitations and revise research strategies responsibly
Present and publish scientific findings with clarity, accuracy and persuasive reasoning
Collaborate across disciplines while demonstrating independence, integrity and responsible research conduct
Vision
To expand understanding of the nervous system and inspire discoveries that improve human health and shape the future of neuroscience.
Values
At the core of our program, we are guided by a commitment to the following values that drive our mission:
Compassion: We act with kindness, empathy and dignity.
Collaboration: We achieve common goals through teamwork and partnerships.
Innovation: We drive transformation by embracing new ideas, discoveries and practices.
Integrity: We do the right thing and commit to accountability in words, actions and use of resources.
Respect: We value everyone and their many perspectives to build trust and a sense of belonging.
Mission
To prepare independent neuroscience scholars through rigorous research, collaborative mentorship and responsible inquiry that advances knowledge and healthcare.
